## Headline

January ran quiet, the way the month after a holiday season tends to. Total spending landed at $4,586.57 across sixty entries — the lightest month in the visible window — and the Tangerine sweep recovered to $400.

## Key findings

Dining tells the story of a month spent mostly at the desk: twenty-three entries for just $258.44, almost all of it the coffee counters between Liberty Village and King West rather than dinners out. Groceries went the other way — $728.10 across ten runs, with four Loblaws Queen West baskets near or over $100 as cooking replaced restaurants. The one distinctive line is a $180 Interac e-transfer to Priya on the 24th: her share of the Prince Edward County cabin deposit for the spring trip.

## Category deep dives

Sports and recreation came to $132 over four classes — three at Solis Movement and one Studio Lagree drop-in — the steadiest the line has looked since fall. Hygiene and household stayed minimal at $110.01 combined. Entertainment was a single Lightbox ticket on the 30th, paired with the month's only LCBO stop and a late Uber home — January's one proper night out.

## Alerts

Toronto Hydro hit $112.46, the winter peak so far. Worth watching February, though the pattern from past years says it eases from here.

## Easy notes

Rent posted at $2,150 on the 1st. Subscriptions held at $55.72. The PRESTO auto-reload went through three times on its usual ten-day rhythm — transit, not the car, is doing the commuting.

## Outlook

February will not be quiet: the Lisbon week is booked for the 6th through the 14th, and the travel line will show it. The cushion January built is about to be spent.
